question: In relation to the structure of proteins:

options.opa: All globular proteins have the same domains.
options.opb: The tertiary structure is present only in oligomeric proteins.
options.opc: Hemoglobin is the only protein that has a quaternary structure.
options.opd: The protein domains are regions of compact folding that exert a certain function.
options.ope: The tertiary and quaternary structures are maintained only by the peptide bonds.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Proteins can have different structures" -> "Globular proteins have unique domains" -> "Tertiary structure can be present in various types of proteins" -> 80% CHAIN: "Proteins can have different structures" -> "Tertiary structure is not exclusive to oligomeric proteins" -> "Hemoglobin is not the only protein with a quaternary structure" -> 70% CHAIN: "Protein domains are regions of compact folding" -> "Protein domains contribute to specific functions" -> "Protein domains are not the same in all proteins" -> 85% CHAIN: "Peptide bonds contribute to maintaining protein structures" -> "Tertiary and quaternary structures are stabilized by various interactions, not just peptide bonds" -> "Peptide bonds alone do not maintain tertiary and quaternary structures" -> 80%
enhanced_information: Globular proteins do not have the same domains; each protein has unique domains. The tertiary structure is not exclusive to oligomeric proteins, and hemoglobin is not the only protein with a quaternary structure. Protein domains are regions of compact folding that contribute to specific functions and vary among proteins. Peptide bonds alone do not maintain tertiary and quaternary structures; various interactions stabilize these structures.
analysis: Globular proteins have unique domains, not the same ones. The tertiary structure can be present in both monomeric and oligomeric proteins. Hemoglobin is not the only protein with a quaternary structure; many proteins exhibit this level of structure. Protein domains are regions of compact folding that perform specific functions and vary among proteins. Tertiary and quaternary structures are stabilized by various interactions, not just peptide bonds.
